latin.497: GAR. Actuale peccatum Adae in homines omnes non minus transit quam corruptio. Nimirum corruptio inhaesione, peccatum Adae reatu & imputatione.
latin.498: PLAC. Itane non minus in homines omnes transit, seu ut loquitur Apostolus, introiit, quam corruptio? Estne igitur peccatum actuale Adami intra nos, non minus quam corruptio? aut potestne intra nos esse, & tamen nobis non inesse, non inhaerere? Imputatio illa extra nos est, in Deo, diuque antequam essemus, facta: actuale quoque Adami peccatum desiit esse aliquot annorum millibus antequam esse inciperemus. Qui igitur dici potest in nos introiisse, & quidem illa imputatione?
latin.499: Deinde convenit inter nos peccatum habituale per unum hominem in omnes homines intrasse, idque ipsa experientia confirmat; sed non convenit peccatum actuale per unum hominem in omnes homines intrasse; hoc enim pernegamus, neque potest probari. Nostra igitur interpretatio negari non potest, cum sit in confesso. Suam igitur qui nobis adversantur, probent interpretationem necesse est, antequam admitti aut possit aut debeat. Denique cum duo illi introeundi modi, quorum alter fingitur, alter est certus & confessus, prorsus sint diversi, alterque alterius respectu, vel nullus vel figuratus sit, qui potest tam diversa unum introeundi verbum semel usurpatum significare?
latin.500: GAR. Cum causam justificationis, non sanctificationis hic tractet Apostolus, nihil mirum est, si ex primaria sua intentione hic potius peccatum actuale Adami, quam corruptionem illam inhaerentem spectare voluerit, cum peccatum ab Adamo patratum, reatus ex illo consequens, respondeat justitiae Christi, & justificationi per eam nostrae: corruptio vero interna, non illi Christi justitiae proprie, sed potius inhaerenti per Spiritum Sanctum in nobis sanctitati respondeat. Qua corruptio quanquam hic etiam propter illam quam diximus connexionem comprehendi potest, non tamen Apostolicum scopum directe respicit, sicut in sequentibus de illa aperte agetur a Paulo.
latin.501: PLAC. Quid? Nonne corruptio est vere peccatum? Nonne ex illa consequitur reatus? Nonne omnes & singulos homines, ne parvulis quidem exceptis adhuc in utero matrum delitescentibus, aeternae mortis reos coram Deo peragit? Nonne ab ea nos imprimis justificari oportet? Mirum est qui nos innovatae doctrinae accusant, tam aperte a recepta ab omnibus Protestantibus doctrina discedere.
latin.502: Deinde planum est peccatum actuale Adami, cum actio fuerit singularis, &, ut tu ipse loqueris, personalis, quae simul ac fuit praeteriit, non potuisse in omnes homines ingredi. Neque potes respondere actionem illam singularem & numero unicam tanto antequam nasceremur admissam in omnes homines imputatione introiisse: quis enim unquam fando audivit hanc phrasim, in aliquem introire, significare, alicui imputari? Noli, quaeso, ut tuam sententiam tuearis vim facere Dei verbo. Actio illa Adami nunquam intra nos fuit, sed neque eius imputatio, quae si ulla esset, Dei actio esset intra Deum manens, non intra nos. Si dixeris actionem illam Adami qua peccatum eius actuale fuit, introiisse in nos dici, non quidem ratione sui, sed ratione poenae quam est nobis commerita, videlicet corruptionis haereditariae, primum rursus abuteris verbo introeundi: nam aliud est poenam peccati aliud peccatum in aliquem intrare. Imputata sunt peccata nostra Christo vadi nostro, nemo tamen dixerit per nos peccata in Christum introiisse, quamvis eorum poenam in se susceperit.

pass_a.497: GAR Cap. VII § IX: Adam's actual passes into all no less than corruption—corruption by inhesion, his sin by reatus and imputation.
pass_a.498: PLAC: Passes—or as Paul says, entered—no less than corruption? Then is Adam's actual inside us as much as corruption? Can it be in us and yet not inhere? That imputation is outside us, in God, done long before we were; Adam's actual ceased millennia before we began. How then entered it into us—and by that imputation?
pass_a.499: We agree habitual sin entered through one man into all—experience confirms it; we do not agree actual entered that way—we deny it flat, and it cannot be proved. Our reading stands as confessed; let opponents prove theirs before it is admitted. Finally the two entry-modes—one feigned, one sure and confessed—are wholly diverse; one beside the other is null or figurative. How can one verb of entering, used once, mean things so unlike?
pass_a.500: GAR: Paul treats justification's cause, not sanctification's—so no wonder if primarily he means Adam's actual rather than inhering corruption: Adam's deed and the reatus from it answer Christ's righteousness and our justification by it; internal corruption answers rather the holiness inhering by the Spirit. Corruption may be folded in by the link we named, yet it is not Paul's direct aim here—he will treat it openly later.
pass_a.501: PLAC: What? Is corruption not truly sin? Does reatus not follow from it? Does it not make every human—even infants still hidden in the womb—guilty of eternal death before God? Must we not first be justified from it? Strange that those who charge us with novelty depart so openly from the doctrine all Protestants receive.
pass_a.502: Next it is plain: Adam's actual, a singular personal act (your own word) that passed as soon as it was, could not enter into all. Nor can you reply that that one numbered deed, done long before we were born, entered by imputation—who ever heard 'to enter into someone' mean 'to be imputed to someone'? Do not wrest God's word to save your view. Adam's act was never inside us, nor would its imputation be (if any)—that would be God's act remaining in God, not in us. If you say the act 'entered' not in itself but by the penalty it earned us (hereditary corruption), you abuse 'enter' again: penalty of sin is one thing, sin entering another. Our sins were imputed to Christ our surety; no one says they entered into him through us, though he bore their penalty. Tip before GAR Resp. 1.

497: GAR. Adam's actual sin passes into all humans no less than corruption. Namely corruption by inhesion, Adam's sin by reatus and imputation.
498: PLAC. Does it then pass into all humans no less, or as the Apostle speaks, enter, than corruption? Is Adam's actual sin therefore inside us, no less than corruption? Or can it be inside us, and yet not be in us, not inhere? That imputation is outside us, in God, and was made long before we were: Adam's actual sin also ceased to be some thousands of years before we began to be. How then can it be said to have entered into us, and indeed by that imputation?
499: Next it is agreed between us that habitual sin entered through one man into all humans, and experience itself confirms it; but it is not agreed that actual sin entered through one man into all humans; for this we flatly deny, and it cannot be proved. Our interpretation therefore cannot be denied, since it is in confession. Those who oppose us must therefore prove their interpretation, before it can or ought to be admitted. Finally since those two modes of entering, of which one is feigned, the other is certain and confessed, are wholly diverse, and one with respect to the other is either nothing or figurative, how can things so diverse be signified by one verb of entering used once?
500: GAR. Since the Apostle here treats the cause of justification, not of sanctification, it is no wonder if from his primary intention he wished here rather to look at Adam's actual sin than at that inhering corruption, since the sin committed by Adam, and the reatus following from it, answers to the righteousness of Christ, and to our justification through it: but internal corruption answers not properly to that righteousness of Christ, but rather to the holiness inhering in us through the Holy Spirit. Which corruption, although here also because of that connection we have named it can be comprehended, yet does not directly regard the Apostolic aim, as in what follows Paul will treat of it openly.
501: PLAC. What? Is corruption not truly sin? Does reatus not follow from it? Does it not make all and each human, not even little ones excepted still hiding in their mothers' womb, guilty of eternal death before God? Must we not first of all be justified from it? It is strange that those who accuse us of innovated doctrine depart so openly from the doctrine received by all Protestants.
502: Next it is plain that Adam's actual sin, since it was a singular action, and, as you yourself speak, personal, which as soon as it was passed away, could not have entered into all humans. Nor can you reply that that singular action and one in number, committed so long before we were born, entered into all humans by imputation: for who ever heard by report that this phrase, to enter into someone, signifies to be imputed to someone? Do not, I ask, to defend your opinion do violence to the word of God. That action of Adam was never inside us, but neither was its imputation, which if any existed would be God's action remaining inside God, not inside us. If you shall say that that action of Adam by which his actual sin was, is said to have entered into us, not indeed by reason of itself, but by reason of the penalty which it earned for us, namely of hereditary corruption, first again you abuse the verb of entering: for it is one thing for the penalty of sin, another for sin, to enter into someone. Our sins were imputed to Christ our surety, yet no one will say that through us sins entered into Christ, although he took their penalty upon himself.
